subtitle: When a coworker's family member dies
description: What to do and what to say when you visit a coworker's family funeral in Korea: picture cards with native audio, workplace Q&A and 21 words.

spine.title: 노선도 · 조문 순서
spine.note: One visit, in order: hear the news, get ready, pay respects, comfort the family, share the meal.

explain.title: 한눈에 · The big picture
explain.why: A Korean funeral usually lasts 3 days in a hospital funeral hall. Coworkers visit to share the family's grief. You do not need many words.

tiles.en: Bow twice to the deceased, once to the family

cards.alt: A phone showing a message with a black mourning ribbon
A message bubble with a black ribbon
cards.ko: 동료에게 '삼가 고인의 명복을 빕니다'라고 메시지를 보내요.
cards.en: I message my coworker: 'May the deceased rest in peace.'

cards.alt: A white condolence envelope marked 부의
cards.ko: 검은 옷을 입고 흰 봉투에 부의금을 넣어요.
cards.en: I wear dark clothes and put condolence money in a white envelope.

cards.alt: An open guestbook with a pen
cards.en: At the funeral hall, I write my name in the guestbook.

cards.ko: 빈소에서 국화를 놓고 두 번 절해요.
cards.en: At the memorial altar, I lay a chrysanthemum and bow twice.

cards.alt: A black mourning armband with white stripes, worn by the chief mourner
cards.ko: 상주에게 한 번 절하고 '얼마나 마음이 아프세요' 하고 조용히 말해요.
cards.en: I bow once to the chief mourner and quietly say, 'You must be heartbroken.'

cards.alt: A bowl of red yukgaejang soup with a spoon
cards.en: I eat a little yukgaejang and leave quietly.

qa.title: 함정 · 헷갈리는 것
qa.note: The two things visitors worry about most.

items.a: 아니요. 종교 때문에 어려우면 묵념만 해도 돼요.
items.aen: No. If bowing is hard for religious reasons, a silent prayer is fine.
items.why: Many Christian families lay a flower and pray in silence instead of bowing.

items.qen: How much condolence money do I give?
items.a: 보통 오만 원이나 십만 원을 내요. 팀 사람들하고 맞춰도 돼요.
items.aen: Usually 50,000 or 100,000 won. You can match the amount with your team.
items.why: Amounts vary by closeness, so ask a teammate. Odd amounts (3, 5 or 7만 원) are the old custom.

qa.title: 회사에서 · At work
qa.small: Questions a teammate may ask you
qa.note: Answer in your head, then tap Listen to compare.

items.aen: It's a hospital funeral hall. Shall we go together?

items.qen: When will you go to pay your respects?

items.aen: The day after tomorrow, in the morning.

qa.title: 막힐 때
qa.small: When you don't know what to say
qa.note: At a funeral, few words are polite. These two are enough.

items.en: I don't know what to say to comfort you.

full_title: 조문 순서 · The visit, start to finish

full.title: 소식 · The news
full.ko: 회사 동료의 아버님이 돌아가셨어요. 동료에게 '삼가 고인의 명복을 빕니다'라고 메시지를 보내요.
full.en: A coworker's father passed away. I message my coworker: 'May the deceased rest in peace.'

full.title: 준비 · Get ready
full.ko: 검은 옷을 입고 흰 봉투에 부의금을 넣어요.
full.en: I wear dark clothes and put condolence money in a white envelope.

full.title: 조문 · At the altar
full.ko: 장례식장에 가서 방명록에 이름을 써요. 빈소에서 국화를 놓고 두 번 절해요.
full.en: At the funeral hall, I write my name in the guestbook. At the memorial altar, I lay a chrysanthemum and bow twice.

full.title: 위로 · Comfort
full.ko: 상주에게 한 번 절하고 '얼마나 마음이 아프세요' 하고 조용히 말해요.
full.en: I bow once to the chief mourner and quietly say, 'You must be heartbroken.'

full.title: 식사 · The meal
full.en: I eat a little yukgaejang and leave quietly.
